text:
Stakeholder Profile

Choose one stakeholder that you would like to think about in more depth. You can choose one of the stakeholders you wrote about in the introductory activity or another stakeholder from your map.

Take a look at the example stakeholder profile below. You will make a stakeholder profile for one of your stakeholders. Like the example, your stakeholder profile will have information about important things in your stakeholder's life, ways they use and enjoy water, and your ideas about why water conservation is important to them.

Stakeholder Profile Instructions

Now that you've read the example, you can make your own stakeholder profile in the sketch box below (or using pencil and paper) following these steps:

1. Create a title for your sketch (for example, "Stakeholder Profile of [Name]")

2. Think of at least three things that are important to this stakeholder. "Important things" might be their values, beliefs, interests, motivations, or anything else important that you know about them. You can draw an image that represents each of your ideas about your stakeholder or search google images and upload each image to the sketch box.

3. Make a caption for each image that explains each thing that is important to your stakeholder. You can use this sentence starter or craft your own sentence(s):

[Thing] is important to [name] because [reason].

4. Think of at least three ways that this stakeholder uses water or ways they could conserve water. Upload one image and one text box caption for each of these ideas and add them the sketch box. For the caption, you can use this sentence starter or craft your own sentence(s):

[Name] uses water to [activity] probably about [number of times a day/week].

[Name] could conserve water by [action].

5. Look over your images and re-read your text boxes. Why is water conservation important to this stakeholder? Add a text box to your sketch to answer these questions. You can use this sentence starter or craft your own sentence(s):

Water conservation is important to [name] because [reason].
Now click the "Idea" button to get suggestions on your Stakeholder profile. After reading those suggestions, did you make any changes? Why did/didn't you make changes?

Examining Assumptions

You probably had to make some assumptions to create this stakeholder profile. In the text box below, note at least two assumptions you made and how you might clarify these assumptions.

Examples:

  • I think Ms. Jones runs the dishwasher in her house every day but I'm not sure because I don't live in her house. She might not even have a dishwasher! I could ask her if she has a dishwasher and how many times she uses it in a week.
  • I think most 8th graders do not turn off the tap when they brush their teeth but I'm not sure. I always turn off the tap because I learned to do this in an assembly last year but I know it is hard to remember so I assume most of the students don't do it. I could ask 8th graders about this but they might say they turn off the water when most times the don't. Maybe if I could ask them anonymously then they might feel comfortable being honest about whether they turn off the water or not.

Now that you have chosen a stakeholder, it is time to understand how water works in the palace where they live and/or work.

Water moves and is used differently depending on where it is. The U.S. Geological Survey created posted that show where water is stored and how it moves in six different types of environments across the country.

Choose ONE environment that matches your stakeholder’s environment (may be where they live and/or work):

  • Urban: Cities and developed areas
  • Agricultural: Farms and crop lands
  • Suburban: Residential neighborhoods
  • Forest: Wooden areas
  • Desert: Dry, arid regions
  • Coast: Where land meets a large body of water like lake, sea, or ocean
Look carefully at your chosen poster. Notice where water is stored, how it moves, and how your stakeholder interacts with (or uses) water in that environment.
In the environment you have chosen, where does water come from in this environment and where is most of the water stored? (i.e., underground, in plants, in lakes, in pipes)
What are the biggest water challenges your stakeholder faces in this environment?
How do the water challenges affect your stakeholders’ daily life or work?

Share about one of the water conservation solutions you read about with a partner. Then discuss the question:

Based on what you have learned from the poster, what is ONE thing your stakeholder needs to know about water in their environment to make better water conservation decisions?

Also, think back to the water usage activity we did in Lesson 1.1.
